best_for: Staff whose company runs its own Mattermost server and who want chat in a desktop window, plus IT teams rolling the client out with an MSI.

points.title: It needs a server
points.text: The desktop app is only a client. On first launch you enter the URL of a Mattermost server, usually from your organization's invite email. Without one there is nothing to sign in to.

points.title: Several servers in one window
points.text: A server dropdown lets you switch between workspaces, and each has tabs for Channels, Boards and Playbooks. The app shows unread badges and desktop notifications and can keep running in the background.

points.title: Free server editions have limits
points.text: Team Edition is free and MIT-licensed, aimed at groups under 250 users without single sign-on. The free Entry edition shows only the last 10,000 channel messages. Paid plans start at Professional; prices are by quote through sales.

points.title: Newer systems only
points.text: Mattermost lists Windows 11, macOS 15 and Ubuntu 22.04 or later for desktop 6.4.0. Server admins on v11.6 or later can also block older app versions from connecting.

points.title: Built for managed rollouts
points.text: The Windows MSI installs for all users on x64 and Arm64. Admins can turn off the built-in updater with the EnableAutoUpdater policy and push versions through SCCM or Intune. The app must sit on a local drive, not a network share.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is unverified
points.text: Mattermost offers .deb, .rpm, AppImage, an APT repository and a tarball. The Flatpak listed here, for x64 and Arm64, is not marked verified on Flathub.

points.title: Old versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 53 versions, handy when a server pins a minimum app version. macOS and Linux list only the current release.
